newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM Howard congratulates Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM Howard congratulates Clinton.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard extended his warmest congratulations on Wednesday to U.S. President Bill Clinton on his re-election.
Howard said he was looking forward to welcoming Clinton and his wife Hillary to Australia later this month.
"Your leadership and that of the nation you have been re-elected to lead are both critical to the peace and stability of the world," Howard wrote in a letter to Clinton.
"I look forward to welcoming you and Mrs Clinton soon to Australia," Howard said in the letter, a copy of which was released here.
"Your visit is an excellent opportunity for us to reaffirm our nations' shared goals and the contribution that our relationship makes to security and growth in our Asia-Pacific region," Howard said.

Clinton is due to arrive in Australia on November 19 for a four day visit, which will see him visit Canberra for talks and relax on Australia's Great Barrier Reef, before flying to the APEC summit in the Philipiines.

Since ousting the 13-year-old Labor administration in March, Australia's conservative government has given priority to reinvigorating ties with Washington, a traditional ally Howard's administration says was neglected by Labor in favour of Asia.
The two countries agreed to boost defence links during top-level talks in Sydney in July, in a move both said would buttress regional peace and security.

But Australia's moves towards closer ties with Washington has attracted criticism from Beijing, which has accused Australia of adopting a U.S. policy of containment towards China. Washington and Australia deny such a policy exists.
